sourceMessages.ui:m_433a4f5a0d5ff619e59b: BPF (Berkeley Packet Filter) is a powerful packet filtering technology that enables efficient packet capture at the kernel level. By applying filters before packets are copied to user space, BPF can significantly reduce CPU usage and improve capture performance.
sourceMessages.ui:m_1193e8f26b65e56b2c66: BPF filters use a simple expression syntax that can match on various packet attributes including:

sourceMessages.ui:m_70270fa1d0f38f4c9365: Charts use retained audit records with usable field values. Field discovery inspects at most the first 100 records of the first available capture; later fields may be absent from the picker. Chart point limits may uniformly sample buckets. Missing or filtered records are not evidence of zero traffic. Numeric fields support line, bar, area, scatter, funnel, and radar charts. Categorical fields support pie, bar, wordcloud, funnel, sankey, and graph visualizations.
